title: Temporal clock-smoothing and bandwidth-aware kernel arbitration for mixed-MIG workloads
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency for mixed-tenant inference on MIG-partitioned H100/L40S nodes by smoothing GPU clock transitions and introducing a bandwidth-aware kernel arbiter that prioritizes attention-prefill kernels without starving decode paths. Motivation: In production we observe p99 spikes when hot prefill workloads contend with bursty decode requests across heterogeneous SKUs (H100, L40S, A10) and mixed MIG topologies. Current kernel selection is static per-model-profile and reacts poorly to clock governor oscillation and nvlink saturation. This ticket introduces a temporal clock-smoothing mechanism plus a runtime arbiter that factors per-request token density, KV cache hit rate, and measured inter-slice bandwidth to select kernel variants and sequence the prefill/decode handoff.
acceptance_criteria: p99 end-to-end latency for conversational workloads decreases by >=12% on benchmark cluster (H100 4xMIG, mixed L40S/A10 load) compared to baseline
No increase in average per-token cost >3% for representative production traces
Arbiter integrates with existing kernel-selector interface and exposes telemetry hooks (kernel_choice, bandwidth_backpressure, clock_state)
Can be toggled via runtime flag and rolled out via canary to <5% of Dedicated fleet
tasks: Bench: reproduce p99 spike with mixed prefill/decode synthetic trace (SLO harness)
Design: define kernel-arbiter scoring function (inputs: token_density, kv_hit, queued_decode_latency, nvlink_bw_headroom, current_clock_state)
Impl: clock-smoothing controller that dampens freq scaling decisions over 200-800ms window
Impl: arbiter module in serving runtime with per-slice bandwidth probe and kernel variant metadata
Perf: run cross-SKU experiments (H100 4xMIG, L40S single, A10 burst) and collect token-level traces
Rollout: create canary plan, fallback policy to legacy selection on regressions
Docs: update runtime-operator guide and console feature flag metadata
notes: Design trade-off: smoothing clock transitions reduces transient p99 but can increase steady-state power usage; we will expose a per-cluster aggressiveness knob to balance power vs latency
Kernel choice policy will prefer prefill attention kernels for prefix-heavy requests when KV cache hit < 30% and queued decode latency > 10ms; otherwise choose lower-power decode-optimized kernels
We avoid cross-slice defragmentation in this phase; future work will consider dynamic MIG rebalancing
Measured NVLink contention is a stronger predictor of p99 than raw GPU frequency in our initial telemetry
Security: no customer model data leaves host; arbiter uses aggregated telemetry only (token counts, cache flags, bandwidth metrics)
telemetry_findings: Baseline: synthetic multi-tenant trace on H100 4xMIG shows 95th=28ms, 99th=112ms for 2048-token workloads
With preliminary smoothing + arbiter prototype we observed 99th=97ms (13% reduction) and 99.9th=184ms -> 22% reduction in worst spikes on 3 runs
Power increase on H100 nodes measured +2.6% avg during steady traffic with smoothing_window=500ms
NVLink probe correlates with p99: correlation coefficient ~0.68 over 8-hour run
KV cache hit-rate threshold tuning: optimal at 28-35% for our sampled traces to avoid decode starvation
